discovery: Discovery that cells organise their interior by liquid-liquid phase separation into biomolecular condensates, and the physical theory of these active droplets

nominees.name: Anthony A. Hyman
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics, Dresden, Germany

nominees.name: Frank Jülicher
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, Germany

subfield: Biological physics / soft condensed matter and statistical physics
motivation: In 2009 Brangwynne, Hyman and Jülicher showed that P granules are liquid droplets that dissolve and condense through phase separation, controlled by concentration gradients. This established that the cell interior is organised by the same physics of phase transitions that governs simple fluids: nucleation, coarsening, wetting, surface tension and critical behaviour. Membraneless compartments such as nucleoli, stress granules and signalling clusters are now understood as condensates whose formation, size and dynamics follow from statistical mechanics. Jülicher and coworkers developed the theory of chemically active droplets, which shows how non-equilibrium reactions suppress Ostwald ripening and set droplet size, and which gives physical mechanisms for cell division and for the origin of life. The discovery connects polymer physics, critical phenomena and biology. It has changed how we think about the cell, and about how protein misfolding and aggregation in neurodegeneration arise from aberrant phase transitions.
